land.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta, 'an autonomous province of Syria' under the French mandate, autonomous under a League statute from November 1937

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the sanjak inside its mandate shape to 1938 and in Turkey from 1939 (17 Turkish and 2 Syrian cells, about 4,750 km2).

land.text: 'By 23 July 1939 ... the territory was fully annexed by Turkey', as Hatay Province

correction.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta (Antakya, Iskenderun, Kirikhan, Payas, Dortyol, Hassa), taken as the Natural Earth province of Hatay

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The land is the difference between the mandate shapes of 1936 (with the sanjak) and 1939 (without): 19 cells, about 4,750 km2. Neither page gives an area. The Hatay page gives a population of 220,000 in 1936 (French High Commission estimate), 39% Turks. The year 1938 begins in September.

region.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta: 'On 2 September 1938, the sanjak assembly proclaimed the Sanjak of Alexandretta as the Hatay State'

ledger.note: 2 September 1938: the assembly proclaims the Hatay State at Antakya. It 'lasted for one year under joint French and Turkish military supervision'; Tayfur Sokmen had arrived in Antakya on 25 August 1938 'appointed by Ataturk to lead the transition', and Turkish forces entered Iskenderun on 5 July 1938 under the 3 July 1938 signings (2,500 troops each for France and Turkey).

region.text: the whole state: 'By 23 July 1939, the last vestiges of the French Mandate authorities had left Antakya, and the territory was fully annexed by Turkey'

ledger.note: 23 July 1939: Hatay is annexed by Turkey. 'On 29 June 1939, following a referendum, the Hatay legislature voted to disestablish the Hatay State and join Turkey'; the Turkish Grand National Assembly approved the law creating Hatay Province on 7 July 1939. The referendum has been called 'phoney' and 'rigged'. The page's infobox gives 29 June (de jure) and 23 July (de facto), the text the reverse.

certainty.note: The old administrative boundary of the sanjak, held since the autonomous regime of 1921 and the League statute of November 1937; neither page describes a survey.

sources.title: Hatay State
sources.note: Proclamation 2 September 1938, vote 29 June 1939, annexation by 23 July 1939, capital, population.

sources.title: Sanjak of Alexandretta
sources.note: Franco-Turkish arrangements of 1937-1938, towns, Tayfur Sokmen, no area.

notes: Written by group me-10-h as a direct counterpart of the French Mandate (loss, 1938) and Turkey (gain, 1939); Cliopatria has no row, the slug is slugify('Hatay State'). The Hatay page gives no area; the 4,750 km2 is the difference between Cliopatria's 1936 and 1939 mandate shapes. The Hatay State was a one-year state under joint French and Turkish supervision; whether it was sovereign is disputed (Syria held that France was obliged to refuse the annexation under the 1936 Franco-Syrian treaty; the page records Hashim al-Atassi's resignation in protest, with no date). Not reached within the two pages: the 1937 League statute in detail (Geneva), the elections of 1938 ('no elections were held' says the Sanjak page, 57,008 voters being registered by 22 July 1938), the flag.
